one_line: A live spreadsheet co-edited by a human and an agent through structured tools.
what_it_does: Provides a seeded workbook where an agent can read and edit ranges, formulas, sorting, filtering, charts, highlights, and export while the human watches the same grid.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured range and workbook state, making precise co-editing substantially more reliable than UI-driving a spreadsheet; the shared live state is central.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes read/write ranges, formulas, sort/filter, charts, highlights, and export on the open grid.
Frame sheet shows the spreadsheet and an Agent Tools/activity panel together with applied-state feedback.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, scoped spreadsheet workflow and the frame sheet shows the grid, agent panel, tool states, and successful-looking updates; end-to-end export is claimed but not visibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a functioning worksheet UI with headers, controls, agent activity, and status feedback.
About text specifies a seeded budget workflow and a Zustand store shared by UI and WebMCP handlers.
impact_rationale: Spreadsheet users have a concrete recurring need for agent assistance with structured transformations while retaining visual oversight; the product addresses that directly.
impact_evidence: Live budget co-editing and formula/sort/chart operations are concrete spreadsheet tasks.
Human-visible changes and confirmation-aware side effects support trustworthy use.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent spreadsheet model is a fresh and well-targeted application of WebMCP, though spreadsheets and AI assistance are established categories.
creativity_evidence: Concept centers on co-editing the open client-side workbook rather than chat-pasted tables or a remote API.
Unified tool/activity surface is pursued across multiple spreadsheet operations.
usability_note: The visible grid plus agent activity panel should make state changes understandable; the breadth of operations may still require careful confirmation.
advance_reason: Strong evidence of a coherent live product with meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A floor-plan editor that continuously audits wheelchair accessibility and can be operated by an agent.
what_it_does: Lets users arrange rooms and furniture, compute reachable routes and doorway clearances, express verdicts in human terms, and export an annotated plan.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to spatial objects and accessibility checks is much more reliable than an agent guessing at canvas interactions; agent and human share the live plan.
leverage_evidence: About text describes continuous route, clearance, overlap, and reachability analysis on the live canvas.
Frame sheet shows a visual workflow/editor with agent-oriented execution states, though text is small.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and unusually specific, with a clear continuous audit model and exportable verdict; the packet and video evidence support a substantial working editor, though exact end-to-end details are not all legible.
execution_evidence: About text specifies four continuous checks and human-readable unreachable-seat counts.
Static implementation is described as a dependency-free canvas application with a deployed demo.
impact_rationale: Accessibility auditing addresses a real safety and inclusion problem for venue and room planners; the demonstrated output is directly actionable for clients and wheelchair users.
impact_evidence: Concrete 90cm route and 150cm doorway-zone requirements.
Exported plan carries the accessibility verdict as a shareable record.
creativity_rationale: Turning a visual floor planner into a continuously reasoning accessibility auditor is a notably original and socially meaningful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Focuses on whole-route reachability rather than only pairwise spacing checks.
Agent-readable structured spatial reasoning is integrated into the planner.
usability_note: Human-language verdicts and direct manipulation are strong; accessibility rules and editing complexity could still be demanding.
advance_reason: High-impact, focused product with strong evidence and substantial structured-state leverage.

one_line: A shared architecture workspace linking system design, cloud estimates, ADRs, and a portable bundle.
what_it_does: Builds C4 models, derives infrastructure needs, compares Azure and AWS estimates, records decisions, and exports a schema-validated .workspec workspace.
leverage_rationale: Agents can manipulate and trace consequences across a complex graph and several durable artifacts through structured state instead of fragile canvas automation; humans review and approve.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly connects the C4 model, infrastructure list, provider comparison, ADR, and export in one shared workflow.
Frame sheet shows the architecture editor and connected graph states with active/success panels.
execution_rationale: The product has an unusually coherent end-to-end architecture workflow and portable output; the frame sheet supports a real editor, while some claimed cloud/ZIP steps are not directly legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a working design canvas with connected nodes and navigation/editor surfaces.
Packet describes schema-validated YAML, import/export, multiple C4 views, and deterministic estimates.
impact_rationale: Architecture teams have a real coordination problem across diagrams, pricing, and decisions; a durable, inspectable workspace directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Explicit problem of fragmented diagrams, estimates, chat rationale, and ADRs.
Portable workspace can be reviewed, committed to Git, or consumed by other tools.
creativity_rationale: The connected design-to-cost-to-decision workflow is a fresh synthesis with meaningful ambition beyond a diagram editor.
creativity_evidence: Combines C4 modeling, provider comparison, and decision records in one artifact lineage.
Human approval is positioned as part of the agent collaboration model.
usability_note: The unified workflow is valuable but inherently information-dense and likely requires onboarding.
advance_reason: Broad but coherent architecture workflow with substantial agent leverage and credible audience value.

one_line: A hands-on lab for inspecting WebMCP authority, approvals, execution, and security receipts.
what_it_does: Presents deliberately vulnerable tool examples and lets people compare presented, declared, and effective surfaces, narrow authority, approve one action, invoke it, and verify the receipt.
leverage_rationale: The product is specifically about structured agent surfaces and cannot be meaningfully replicated by generic UI automation; native tools, authorization, and receipts are the subject of the experience.
leverage_evidence: About text defines a public URL → native tool → human review → narrow approval → invocation → verified receipt protocol.
Frame sheet shows the lab's account-check UI and agent/browser workflow, though exact receipt text is small.
execution_rationale: The lessons and security protocol are clearly scoped and intentional, with multiple vulnerability classes and a concrete verification loop; the contact sheet does not make every final receipt legible.
execution_evidence: About text lists read-only mutation, overbroad schemas, instruction-shaped output, and vague confirmation lessons.
Packet reports a deployed public lab with four gallery images and video evidence.
impact_rationale: As agent-native sites emerge, developers and users need practical ways to understand authority and verify side effects; this lab provides direct educational and security value.
impact_evidence: Three-surface comparison—presented, declared, effective—is a concrete security model.
Narrow approval and security receipts address real agent trust failures.
creativity_rationale: A synthetic security test range that teaches WebMCP through deliberately mismatched surfaces is highly original and deeply aligned with the medium.
creativity_evidence: Turns WebMCP security concerns into interactive experiments rather than an article.
Protocol separates human approval from agent capability and verifies actual effect.
usability_note: Lesson-based inspection and receipts are likely understandable; security concepts may still challenge beginners.
red_flags: Frame text is too small to independently verify every receipt state.
advance_reason: Exceptionally strong WebMCP-specific concept with credible educational/security impact.

one_line: A browser CAD system where agents create and edit precise, 3D-printable parts through structured tools.
what_it_does: Provides editable multi-part CAD geometry, inspection, profiles, features, booleans, patterns, assembly operations, and export for manufacturing.
leverage_rationale: Precise topology, dimensions, faces, and parametric operations are impractical to control reliably through generic pointer automation; structured CAD state is central.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 35 tools spanning scene inspection, exact geometry, features, booleans, and assembly.
Frame sheet shows an agent-driven build flow progressing from prompt to generated visual preview.
execution_rationale: The demonstrated scope is ambitious and the frame sheet shows progression to a rendered preview; claims about manufacturing/export are broader than what is visibly proven.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows prompt, agent progress, and a live visual preview/result.
Packet describes an editable CAD scene rather than isolated mesh generation and gives a concrete tool chain.
impact_rationale: CAD is a real barrier for makers and engineers; making precise editable, printable parts accessible through natural-language collaboration has credible value.
impact_evidence: Explicit goal is real 3D-printable objects, not just text-to-mesh output.
Tools cover modification and inspection needed for iterative design.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native parametric CAD with topology-aware structured operations is an ambitious and memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Exposes real CAD workflow semantics such as faces, edges, fillets, shells, booleans, and mates.
Combines natural-language design with human-editable geometry.
usability_note: Natural language lowers the CAD barrier, but precise geometry and a broad operation set remain complex.
red_flags: Manufacturing validity and export quality are claimed more strongly than visibly verified in the contact sheet.
advance_reason: One of the clearest transformative WebMCP use cases, with visible generated-product progression.

one_line: A procurement replay where changing evidence cannot silently inherit yesterday's approval or capacity.
what_it_does: Recommends a bid, requires exact snapshot approval, issues bounded permits, and retests after evidence changes while failing closed on conflicts.
leverage_rationale: Structured evidence revisions, decision revisions, permits, and failed-closed capacity state are precisely the shared state that generic UI automation cannot safely preserve.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five page-owned tools, approval_required, no agent approval endpoint, exact snapshot checkpoint, and seven-call flight recorder.
Frame sheet visibly presents the £900k qualification narrative and zero-hours outcome, but not the full tool log.
execution_rationale: The synthetic two-act protocol is unusually explicit and coherent, with a clear failed-closed outcome; visual evidence is more landing-page/storyboard-like than a full run.
execution_evidence: Packet gives a deterministic scenario with concrete bids, gates, revisions, and zero committed capacity.
About text distinguishes agent tools from the human checkpoint and specifies the conflict result.
impact_rationale: Approval drift and stale authority are real risks in procurement and other consequential workflows; the product demonstrates a credible safeguard pattern.
impact_evidence: Active permit conflict preserves the £750k/32-hour permit and moves zero hours.
Exact evidence and decision revisions are retained for later re-proof.
creativity_rationale: Starting where approval demos usually stop—after facts change and authority might drift—is a novel, memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Core concept is temporal authority invalidation under changing evidence.
Human checkpoint is deliberately not exposed as an agent tool.
usability_note: The protocol is safety-conscious but may be conceptually demanding for users unfamiliar with revisioned approvals.
red_flags: The viewed frame sheet is largely promotional/hero presentation and does not visibly prove the full seven-call flow.
advance_reason: Highly original and consequential protocol; advance despite thinner direct motion evidence.

one_line: A resume tailoring workflow where an agent proposes diffs and the human accepts or rejects them.
what_it_does: Analyzes a job and resume, identifies gaps, scores coverage, proposes bullet and cover-letter changes, and exports only accepted edits.
leverage_rationale: Shared page state and structured proposal/diff tools improve reliability and consent, but a capable general agent could achieve much of the same outcome with meaningful UI friction.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheet shows ResumeMatch input cards, agent progress, file selection, and populated inputs.
About text says tools read the live job/resume and every rewrite appears as a diff requiring human acceptance.
execution_rationale: The central intake-to-proposal-to-review concept is coherent, with visible progression through uploads and populated inputs; final export is claimed rather than visibly shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows upload, job-description, profile, and agent workflow states.
About text specifies FastAPI/SQLite implementation, capped model calls, diffs, and accepted-only export.
impact_rationale: Job seekers have a real need for tailored materials, and preserving personal truth and human approval addresses a meaningful trust concern.
impact_evidence: Concrete resume/job matching, ATS coverage, gap finding, and bullet rewriting workflow.
Reject/accept controls prevent silent replacement of experience.
creativity_rationale: Human-approved resume diffs are a thoughtful trust-oriented angle on a familiar AI writing category.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes changes on the actual bullet with visible before/after diff.
Accepted-only review/export creates a deliberate consent interaction.
usability_note: Diff review and explicit acceptance are clear; document intake and multiple analyses add some workflow weight.
red_flags: Viewed frames do not visibly show the final diff or export state.
advance_reason: Coherent and useful workflow with visible product progression and a strong human-control design.

one_line: A conversational 3D room designer where agents place catalog furniture into a live spatial scene.
what_it_does: Lets users browse furniture, place and transform pieces, manage finishes, and receive spatial advice while agents inspect and update the shared room state.
leverage_rationale: Structured catalog IDs, scene-instance IDs, dimensions, collision, and live room state make agent placement safer and more precise than clicking through a 3D canvas.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheet progresses from conversational landing page to a 3D editor with visible furniture changes and selection state.
About text specifies catalog search, placement, updates, removal, finishes, and spatial advice tools.
execution_rationale: The visible editor demonstrates a coherent room-design experience with furniture in a 3D scene; full collision/advice behavior is described but not fully legible in frames.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a live 3D room with multiple furniture pieces and successive layout states.
About text describes Zustand synchronization, boundary/collision logic, and catalog-backed assets.
impact_rationale: Home designers and decor hobbyists have a real visual planning need; live placement and advice provide credible value, though the audience/problem is less consequential than accessibility or safety products.
impact_evidence: Concrete catalog, layout, lighting, flow, and clearance use cases.
Agent can react to human changes in the same room scene.
creativity_rationale: Conversational control of a constrained 3D room with catalog-grounded objects is a fresh synthesis of interior design and agent collaboration.
creativity_evidence: Separates catalog IDs from scene-instance IDs and accounts for rotated footprints.
Combines natural-language design with direct manipulation and spatial constraints.
usability_note: The visual scene is approachable and direct manipulation helps; 3D spatial editing can still be cognitively demanding.
advance_reason: Visible, coherent 3D product with meaningful structured spatial-state leverage.

one_line: An AI-controllable physics lab for running, measuring, and comparing live experiments.
what_it_does: Offers projectile and mass-spring simulations, visual aids, measurements, trial notebooks, comparisons, and native tools for configuring and controlling experiments.
leverage_rationale: Semantic experiment controls and precise measurements let an agent operate the simulation and inspect live state more reliably than generic UI control; shared trials enable collaboration.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools to configure, run, pause, measure, and compare experiments.
Frame sheet visibly shows the Trajectory Lab UI and a storyboard of launch/measurement concepts, though no explicit tool log.
execution_rationale: The lab has a clear educational scope and the visible simulation UI is coherent, but the viewed frame sheet does not clearly show a completed run with numerical results.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a dark Trajectory Lab with simulation area and controls.
About text describes physics engine, live measurements, trial history, and consistency between visual and tool data.
impact_rationale: Students and educators have a clear need for experiment-based understanding; controllable simulations and recorded comparisons credibly support learning.
impact_evidence: Projectile and mass-spring experiments expose measurable concepts rather than static explanations.
Recorded notebooks and comparisons support iterative inquiry.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP as a shared experimental instrument, including event-focused pauses such as apex/equilibrium, is an original educational interaction.
creativity_evidence: Agent can run, pause, measure, and compare the same live experiment a human sees.
Design emphasizes scientific actions rather than button automation.
usability_note: Visual simulation and measurement aids support learning; multiple parameters and modes may require guidance.
red_flags: The viewed frame sheet communicates the concept but does not visibly prove an agent invocation or completed measurement result.
advance_reason: Strong educational concept and credible product UI, with confidence reduced for thin direct invocation/result evidence.

one_line: A real cleaning intake and booking flow exposed as structured WebMCP tools with customer approval retained.
what_it_does: Collects cleaning details, calculates estimates, finds appointment options, selects a time, and prepares a visible exact review for final approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools remove the repeated find/scroll/click/type burden from a long conditional production form while preserving shared state; this is more than a cosmetic wrapper.
leverage_evidence: About text contrasts previous browser automation with eight structured tools and a shared customer-intake context.
Frame sheet explicitly depicts FIND, SCROLL, CLICK, TYPE and one shared state across the booking workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a real production-derived flow and the frame sheet shows the form being navigated through multiple states; final booking confirmation is intentionally not shown.
execution_evidence: About text says customers complete the production quote form daily and the flow covers 57 questions.
Frame sheet shows the cleaning form, repeated navigation states, and a shared-state message.
impact_rationale: This addresses a concrete accessibility and completion barrier for cleaning customers, including seniors and less computer-comfortable users, and is grounded in a real business workflow.
impact_evidence: Real customer intake reportedly occurs two or three times daily.
Conversation-speed interaction reduces burden while retaining visible review and final customer approval.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a real, lengthy service-booking flow is a strong practical synthesis, though the booking category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Reframes an existing AI-automated form from browser actions to semantic tools.
Same tool surface supports both customer booking and regression testing.
usability_note: Shared context and conversational intake directly target form fatigue; visible review before approval is a strong usability safeguard.
red_flags: Contact sheet does not visibly show a completed appointment confirmation, only intake progression.
advance_reason: High practical impact and credible execution evidence for a real business workflow.
